note: Every number here is a documented, editable assumption. They are the reason the system can estimate real-world size from a single photograph with no measuring equipment (requirement 8).

reference_objects.label: Main door height
reference_objects.note: Standard Indian residential door leaf is 2100 mm (6 ft 11 in) including frame. The most reliable reference in a facade photo.

reference_objects.label: Floor-to-floor height
reference_objects.note: Typical low-rise residential floor-to-floor is 3.0-3.2 m. Use when a door is not visible.

reference_objects.label: Window height
reference_objects.note: Common 1200 mm window. Weakest of the three - window sizes vary a lot.

reference_objects.label: Something I measured myself
reference_objects.note: Best accuracy. Measure any visible edge with a tape and enter it.

measurement.note: Linear items are measured along their polyline in running feet. Railing height is only used to sanity-check the drawn polyline, not to bill area.

cost_settings.note: Scaffolding is charged on total painted/clad area. Overhead and GST are applied in that order on the running subtotal.

limitations: Areas are derived from a single photograph. Faces of the building not visible in the photo are not measured and are not in the estimate.
Perspective rectification assumes each wall is planar and roughly rectangular. Curved or heavily ornamented facades will be over- or under-estimated.
The automatic region detection is a starting suggestion, not a survey. Reviewing and correcting it is a required step, not an optional one.
Material rates are regional and volatile. The seeded catalog is a midpoint of public 2026 listings and is meant to be overwritten with your own quotations.
Cost output is advisory and is not a quotation or a legally binding estimate.
